name: Vikas Khanna
bio: Vikas Khanna is an Indian chef, restaurateur, cookbook writer, filmmaker and humanitarian. He has been a judge on MasterChef India since its first season and is based in New York City.

recipes.name: Paneer Tikka
recipes.description: Cubes of paneer marinated in hung curd and smoky spices, then charred with peppers and onion. A tandoor classic that works just as well under a hot grill.
ingredients: 400 g paneer, cut into 3 cm cubes
1 tsp chaat masala, plus extra to finish
1 green bell pepper and 1 red onion, cut into squares
steps: Whisk the yogurt with ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala, chaat masala, kasuri methi, gram flour, mustard oil, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Fold in the paneer, pepper and onion so every piece is coated. Cover and rest in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Thread paneer and vegetables alternately onto soaked skewers.
Grill on a hot pan, under a broiler or over charcoal for 12-15 minutes, turning once, until the edges blister and char.
Dust with chaat masala, squeeze over lemon and serve hot with mint chutney.

recipes.name: Chole Bhature
recipes.description: Dark, tangy Punjabi chickpeas simmered with tea and whole spices, served with puffed, pillowy bhature. Weekend food in the best possible sense.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 bay leaves, 1 black cardamom
3 tbsp oil, plus more for frying
1/2 cup yogurt and 1/2 tsp baking soda
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked chickpeas with the tea bag, bay leaves, black cardamom and salt until very soft, about 20 minutes. Discard the tea bag.
Knead flour, semolina, yogurt, baking soda, a pinch of salt and a little water into a soft dough. Oil the surface, cover and rest for 1 hour.
Heat oil, crackle cumin, then fry the onions until deep golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until fragrant.
Add tomato puree and chole masala and cook until the oil separates. Tip in the chickpeas with their cooking liquid and simmer 20 minutes, mashing a few to thicken.
Finish with amchur. Roll the dough into ovals and deep-fry in hot oil, pressing gently so they puff.
Serve the chole with bhature, sliced onion, green chilli and a wedge of lemon.

recipes.name: Mutton Rogan Josh
recipes.description: A Kashmiri lamb curry coloured deep red with Kashmiri chillies and ratan jot, with fennel and dry ginger instead of onions and garlic doing the heavy lifting.
ingredients: 800 g bone-in mutton, cut into pieces
4 green cardamom, 2 black cardamom, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves
2 onions, sliced (optional, for a Punjabi-style gravy)
steps: Heat the oil until it just smokes, lower the heat and add the whole spices and asafoetida.
Add the mutton and sear on high heat for 8-10 minutes until browned all over.
Mix the chilli powder with a little water to a paste and add it to the pan; this is what gives rogan josh its colour without burning.
Add the yogurt a spoon at a time, stirring constantly so it does not split. Add onions and tomatoes if using.
Stir in fennel and ginger powder, salt and 2 cups of hot water. Cover and simmer 60 minutes, or pressure-cook 25 minutes, until the meat falls off the bone.
Reduce the gravy until the oil floats on top and serve with steamed rice.

name: Pooja Dhingra
bio: Pooja Dhingra is an Indian pastry chef and entrepreneur. She opened India's first macaron store and founded Le15 Patisserie, a bakery chain known for macarons and French desserts.

recipes.name: Tandoori Chicken
recipes.description: Chicken legs scored and marinated twice, first in lemon and then in spiced yogurt, so the flavour reaches the bone. Finish over a flame for the smoke.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken legs and thighs, skin removed
1 tsp each: cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala
Mint chutney, onion rings and lemon wedges to serve
steps: Make deep cuts in the chicken. Rub with lemon juice, half the chilli powder and salt and rest for 20 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt with the remaining spices, ginger-garlic paste, kasuri methi and mustard oil. Coat the chicken thoroughly and marinate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat the oven to 220 C. Place the chicken on a rack over a tray and roast 20 minutes.
Turn, baste with the leftover marinade and roast another 15-20 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through.
For smokiness, hold a piece over a gas flame for a few seconds or finish on a hot grill.
Serve with mint chutney, onion rings and lemon.

recipes.name: Aloo Paratha
recipes.description: Whole-wheat flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potato and cooked in ghee until blistered. Breakfast across North India, best with white butter and curd.
ingredients: 1 tsp each: cumin seeds, coriander powder, amchur
A handful of chopped coriander leaves
steps: Knead the flour with a pinch of salt and water into a soft, smooth dough. Rest for 20 minutes.
Mix the mashed potato with onion, chilli, ginger, spices, coriander and salt. Taste and adjust.
Divide dough and filling into 8 portions. Roll a dough ball into a small disc, place filling in the centre, gather the edges and seal.
Dust with flour and roll gently into a 15 cm round, keeping the pressure even so the filling does not tear through.
Cook on a hot tawa 1 minute per side, then brush with ghee and cook until golden spots appear on both sides.
Serve hot with curd, pickle and a knob of butter.

recipes.name: Paneer Butter Masala
recipes.description: Soft paneer in a silky tomato and cashew gravy finished with butter, cream and kasuri methi. The restaurant favourite, made gently sweet rather than heavy.
ingredients: 1 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp coriander powder
steps: Melt 1 tbsp butter with the oil, soften the onion, then add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes and cashews. Cook 10 minutes until the tomatoes collapse.
Cool slightly, blend to a smooth puree and pass through a sieve for a silky texture.
Return to the pan with the remaining butter. Add chilli powder, coriander powder, sugar and salt and simmer 10 minutes until glossy.
Add 1/2 cup water and the paneer and simmer gently 5 minutes so the paneer softens.
Finish with garam masala, cream and kasuri methi. Serve with naan or jeera rice.

name: Ranveer Brar
bio: Ranveer Singh Brar is an Indian celebrity chef, MasterChef India judge, author, restaurateur and food historian known for his storytelling around regional Indian food.

recipes.name: Butter Chicken
recipes.description: Murgh makhani the Delhi way: tandoori-style chicken folded into a buttery tomato gravy that is tangy, lightly sweet and smoky. Not a dish to rush.
ingredients: 1/2 cup yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp chilli powder (marinade)
steps: Marinate the chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder and salt for at least 1 hour.
Grill or pan-sear the chicken on high heat until charred in spots but not fully cooked through. Set aside.
Simmer tomatoes and cashews with 1 cup water for 15 minutes, then blend smooth and strain.
Melt butter, add the chilli powder and immediately pour in the tomato puree. Season and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and its juices, honey and garam masala and simmer 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked.
Stir in cream and kasuri methi, swirl in a little more butter and serve with butter naan.

recipes.name: Palak Paneer
recipes.description: Bright green spinach gravy with soft paneer, kept vivid by blanching the leaves and never overcooking them. Lighter than it looks and ready in half an hour.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp garam masala and 1/2 tsp turmeric
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 90 seconds, then plunge into iced water to keep the colour. Blend with the green chillies to a smooth puree.
Heat ghee, crackle the cumin seeds and fry the onion until soft and golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, then tomatoes and turmeric. Cook until the tomatoes break down.
Pour in the spinach puree, season and simmer just 3-4 minutes. Longer and it turns dull.
Add paneer and garam masala and heat through. Finish with cream and serve with roti.

recipes.name: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
recipes.description: Kacchi-style biryani where raw marinated chicken and parboiled basmati are layered and sealed with dough, then cooked on dum until the rice steams in the meat's juices.
ingredients: 3 cups aged basmati rice, soaked 30 minutes
3 onions, thinly sliced and fried until crisp (birista)
A large handful each of mint and coriander
2 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp biryani masala
Whole spices: 2 bay leaves, 4 cardamom, 6 cloves, 1 cinnamon, 1 star anise, 1 tsp shahi jeera
A pinch of saffron soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk
steps: Marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chillies, half the fried onions, half the herbs, the ground spices, lemon juice, oil and salt. Rest 2 hours or overnight.
Boil a large pot of water with the whole spices and plenty of salt. Cook the rice until 70% done (a grain should break with slight resistance) and drain.
Spread the marinated chicken in a heavy-bottomed pot. Layer the rice on top, then scatter the remaining fried onions, herbs, saffron milk and ghee.
Seal the lid with a rope of dough or a tight foil wrap. Cook on high heat for 10 minutes, then on the lowest heat (ideally over a tawa) for 35-40 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes before opening. Fluff gently from the sides so the layers stay intact.
Serve with mirchi ka salan and raita.

name: Shipra Khanna
bio: Shipra Khanna is an Indian celebrity chef, restaurateur, author and television personality. She won the second season of MasterChef India at the age of 29.

recipes.name: Vegetable Pulao
recipes.description: Fragrant basmati cooked with whole spices, seasonal vegetables and ghee-toasted cashews. A one-pot rice for when biryani is too much effort.
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas, cauliflower)
1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 3 green cardamom, 1 cinnamon stick
steps: Heat the ghee and toast the cashews until golden; lift them out and set aside.
In the same ghee, crackle the cumin and whole spices, then fry the onion until light golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, chillies and the vegetables. Saute 3 minutes.
Add the drained rice and stir gently for a minute so each grain is coated in ghee.
Pour in the water, add mint and salt, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Fluff with a fork, top with cashews and serve with raita.

recipes.name: Amritsari Chole
recipes.description: The Amritsar version of chickpea curry: darker, drier and more sour, with a tempering of ghee and ginger poured over at the end. Eat with kulcha or bhature.
ingredients: 2 tbsp black tea leaves tied in muslin, or 2 tea bags
2.5 cm ginger, julienned, and 2 green chillies, slit, for tempering
steps: Pressure-cook the chickpeas with the tea bundle and salt until completely soft. Remove the tea.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee and fry the onions until deep brown, a good 12 minutes. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, chole masala, anardana, amchur and black salt. Cook until the mixture is thick and the ghee separates.
Add the chickpeas with a little of their liquid and mash about a quarter of them. Simmer 20 minutes until the gravy clings to the chickpeas.
Heat the remaining ghee, sizzle the ginger and chillies for 30 seconds and pour over the chole.
Serve with kulcha or bhature and sliced onion.

recipes.name: Gulab Jamun
recipes.description: Soft milk-solid dumplings fried slowly to a deep brown and soaked in cardamom and rose syrup. The trick is a very low frying temperature and patience.
ingredients: 1 tbsp ghee, plus more for frying
steps: Boil the sugar and water with cardamom and saffron for 5 minutes until slightly sticky but not thick. Add rose water and keep warm.
Mix milk powder, flour, semolina and baking soda. Rub in the ghee, then add milk a spoon at a time to form a soft, slightly sticky dough. Do not knead.
Grease your palms and roll into smooth, crack-free balls about 2.5 cm across.
Heat ghee on low; a test ball should rise slowly. Fry in batches, stirring the ghee gently so they brown evenly, 8-10 minutes until deep brown.
Drop the hot jamuns into the warm syrup and soak at least 2 hours. They will double in size.
Serve warm or at room temperature, topped with pistachios.

name: Sanjeev Kapoor
bio: Sanjeev Kapoor is an Indian celebrity chef, entrepreneur and television personality. He hosted Khana Khazana, the longest-running show of its kind in Asia, broadcast in 120 countries.

recipes.name: Tandoori Roti
recipes.description: A thick, chewy whole-wheat bread slapped onto the wall of a tandoor. At home, an inverted pressure-cooker or a very hot tawa gives you the same blistered surface.
steps: Mix flour, salt and sugar. Add yogurt and oil, then water gradually to form a soft dough. Knead 8 minutes until smooth and rest 30 minutes under a damp cloth.
Divide into 8 balls. Roll each into a 6 mm thick round, slightly thicker than a chapati.
Heat a tawa until very hot. Brush one side of the roti with water and press the wet side onto the tawa so it sticks.
When bubbles appear, flip the whole tawa over the open flame (or hold the roti over the flame with tongs) so the top blisters and chars.
Lift off with a spatula, brush with ghee and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Goan Fish Curry
recipes.description: A coastal curry of firm fish in a coconut, tamarind and red chilli gravy, sharp with kokum. Serve with plain steamed rice and nothing else.
ingredients: 600 g firm fish steaks (kingfish, pomfret or seer)
1 tbsp coriander seeds and 1 tsp cumin seeds
A small ball of tamarind soaked in warm water, or 4 kokum petals
steps: Rub the fish with salt and a pinch of turmeric and rest 15 minutes.
Grind the coconut, soaked chillies, coriander, cumin, turmeric, peppercorns, garlic and ginger with a little water to a very smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil, soften the onion, then add tomatoes and cook until pulpy.
Add the ground masala and fry 5 minutes until it smells toasty. Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind extract, season and bring to a gentle simmer.
Slide in the fish and cook 8-10 minutes without stirring, spooning gravy over the pieces, until just cooked through.
Rest 10 minutes before serving with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Rajma Chawal
recipes.description: Kidney beans slow-simmered in a thick onion-tomato gravy and ladled over steamed rice. The comfort meal of every North Indian household, improved by a day in the fridge.
ingredients: 1.5 cups dried rajma (kidney beans), soaked overnight
1 tsp each: coriander powder, red chilli powder
1/2 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp garam masala
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked rajma with salt and 4 cups water until soft enough to crush between two fingers, about 20 minutes.
Heat ghee, crackle the cumin and fry the onions until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and chillies.
Add the tomato puree and powdered spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add the rajma with its cooking liquid, mash a few beans against the pan and simmer 20 minutes until thick and creamy.
Finish with garam masala and coriander and serve over hot steamed rice.

name: Pankaj Bhadouria
bio: Pankaj Bhadouria won the first season of MasterChef India after leaving a 16-year teaching career. She has since hosted several cookery shows including Chef Pankaj Ka Zayka and Kifayati Kitchen.

recipes.name: Dal Makhani
recipes.description: Whole black lentils and kidney beans simmered for hours until they turn creamy on their own, then enriched with butter and a little cream. Patience is the main ingredient.
ingredients: 1 cup whole black lentils (sabut urad), soaked overnight
A piece of charcoal for smoking (optional)
steps: Pressure-cook the lentils and beans with salt and 5 cups water for 30 minutes, then simmer uncovered on low for 1 hour, stirring and mashing against the sides until creamy.
In another pan melt 2 tbsp butter, add ginger-garlic paste, then tomato puree and chilli powder. Cook until thick.
Add the tomato masala to the lentils and keep simmering on the lowest heat for another hour, adding hot water as needed. The longer the better.
Stir in the remaining butter, cream, garam masala and kasuri methi.
For a dhaba finish, place a hot piece of charcoal in a small bowl in the pot, drizzle with ghee, cover for 5 minutes, then remove.
Serve with naan or jeera rice, with a swirl of cream on top.

recipes.name: Pav Bhaji
recipes.description: Mumbai's great street food: a buttery mash of vegetables cooked down with pav bhaji masala, served with soft buns toasted in more butter, raw onion and lime.
ingredients: 1 cup cauliflower florets and 1/2 cup green peas, boiled
5 tbsp butter, plus more for the pav
Chopped coriander, lime wedges and chopped onion to serve
steps: Melt 3 tbsp butter, fry the onions until soft, then add ginger-garlic paste and capsicum.
Add tomatoes, chilli powder and salt and cook until mushy.
Add the boiled vegetables and pav bhaji masala. Mash everything together with a potato masher, adding a splash of water, and cook 10 minutes until thick and glossy.
Stir in 2 tbsp butter and coriander.
Slit the pav, butter generously and toast on the tawa with a pinch of masala until golden.
Serve the bhaji topped with a cube of butter, with the pav, raw onion and lime.

recipes.name: Rasgulla
recipes.description: Bengal's spongy chhena dumplings, boiled in light sugar syrup until they swell and turn snow white. The chhena must be kneaded until it feels like soft clay.
ingredients: 2 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar diluted in 2 tbsp water
1 tsp fine semolina or all-purpose flour
steps: Bring the milk to a boil, switch off the heat and add the diluted lemon juice a little at a time until the milk splits completely and the whey turns clear.
Strain through muslin, rinse under cold water to remove the sourness and hang for 30 minutes so it drains but stays moist.
Knead the chhena with the semolina using the heel of your palm for 8-10 minutes until smooth and slightly greasy. Roll into 12 small crack-free balls.
Boil the sugar, water and cardamom in a wide pan. Drop in the balls, cover and boil on high for 15 minutes, splashing in a little water every 5 minutes to keep the syrup thin.
They will double in size. Switch off, add rose water and cool in the syrup.
Chill for at least 4 hours before serving.
